belief: God doesn't hear my prayers, or He would have taken this away.
origins: After praying for months or years for relief, silence can feel like rejection. Some conclude that God is not listening or does not care.
teaches: Paul prayed three times and received a “no” with a better promise: “My grace is sufficient for you.” “The Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.” Jesus prayed in Gethsemane, “Yet not My will, but Yours be done” (Luke 22:42). “He has not despised or detested the torment of the afflicted… but has attended to his cry for help.” God hears every prayer. His answers are sometimes “wait,” “no,” or “here is strength instead.”
self_statements: My prayers bounce off the ceiling.
He could heal me if He wanted.
errors: Believing God either answers my way or does not hear.
Feeling unheard and concluding that He is not listening.
questions: What have I prayed for, and how long?
What has God provided that I did not ask for?
What do Paul and Jesus teach about unanswered prayer?
How does the Spirit help me pray?
What would trust look like if the answer is “not now” or “no”?
truth: God hears every prayer, even when He does not give the answer I ask for. He may give grace, strength, or a different path. I can keep praying and trust His care.
log: Each week, note one prayer and one provision.
prayer: Lord, I have prayed and still hurt. Hear me, help me in my weakness, and give me trust to wait for Your answer. Amen.
